text: A workspace is where every dashboard, report, and semantic model covered in this entire chapter actually lives — the single collaborative container everything else in the Power BI service builds on top of.

Here's a real workspace's content list — a dashboard, a report, a workbook, and a dataset, all grouped together in one place. Everything you've published anywhere in this course so far sits inside a workspace looking exactly like this one.

Creating a new workspace only takes a unique name, plus a handful of optional settings you can fill in or skip — a contact list for notifications, a workspace image, a linked Microsoft 365 OneDrive. All of these settings live under Workspace settings, reachable at any time from the three-dot menu next to the workspace's name.

Four distinct roles control what colleagues can actually do inside your workspace once you add them. Admin has complete control over everything, including deleting the workspace itself. Member can publish and update content, and add other members too. Contributor can add, edit, and publish content, but can't manage who else has access. And Viewer can only look at what's already there, with no editing or publishing rights at all.

If you regularly work across several different workspaces, pin your favorites to the top of the workspace flyout list — a small detail, but one that genuinely saves real time once you're juggling more than a couple of them.

One warning worth taking seriously before you move on: deleting a workspace is completely permanent, with no recycle bin and no recovery of any kind — every dashboard, report, and semantic model inside it disappears for good. Lesson 70 covers exactly what happens the moment you actually publish something into one.
